note: Two expert pentatonic runs from the runs book, one per section: the run from Mi to the high Do, then the riff that opens on a held Sol. Each pass climbs a semitone to the top of the voice, and the tempo is a move (70 up to 100), so the drill gets faster without a copy. Folded in from the to-the-top and pentatonic-riff drills.

exercise.title: A fast pentatonic run
exercise.why: The run leaves out Fa and Ti, the two notes that sit a half step from a neighbour, so every note has room and the run stays clear when it gets fast.

cells.heading: From Mi to the high Do

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the run: two chords set the key, and the mic starts with them. The run starts on {{3}}, climbs to the high {{1}} and comes back down to the {{6}} under Do, four notes per beat. Each pass starts a semitone higher, and the last one reaches the top of your range.
Sing it lightly on "ah", and move to "oo" when a pass feels tight.

Press Play below to hear the next run. It holds {{5}} for a beat, turns up to the high {{1}} and runs down to Do, then dips to the {{6}} under it. Tune the held {{5}} first, then let the fast notes leave from it, on "ah".
Practice until the passes stay clear right up to the top of your range.
